title: Wide-lot subdivision and Stanley Avenue townhouse proposal
subtitle: Also covered: Clara Way private street naming, a climate lens for council reports, and Bridge Street traffic concerns.
overview: The committee recommended that Council approve zoning changes and modified draft plans for the Kitchener Green subdivision near Bleams and Trussler roads {{vote:m3}}. The changes allow wider, shallower lots. Staff said overall unit numbers stay broadly similar and that more parkland will be conveyed to the City.

For the proposed semi-detached and townhouse development at 26 Stanley Avenue and 31 Schweitzer Street, the committee recommended referring the matter to the August 24, 2026 Council meeting {{vote:m4}}. This gives staff time to review parkland improvements at Schaefer Park and to keep discussing traffic concerns with the Region. Nearby residents raised concerns about traffic, density, tree removal and the adjacent cemetery.

The committee also recommended acknowledging Clara Way as the private street name at 60 Trussler Road {{vote:m1}}. It recommended that staff consider a climate lens, focused on greenhouse gas emission reductions, in the next review of the corporate report template {{vote:m2}}. Council will make the final decisions on all of these items.

decisions.item: Kitchener Green zoning and draft plan changes
decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving the zoning by-law amendment and major modifications to two draft plans of subdivision for the Kitchener Green lands, subject to the conditions in the staff report.

The committee recommended referring the zoning and vacant land condominium recommendation to the August 24, 2026 Council meeting so staff can review Schaefer Park improvements and continue talks with the Region on traffic.
The committee recommended acknowledging the name Clara Way for private streets in the multiple residential development and directing Legal Services to advertise and prepare the by-law.

The committee recommended that staff consider a climate lens, specifically greenhouse gas emission reductions, in the next corporate report template review and add a climate item to Council reports where appropriate.

debate: On the Kitchener Green lots, the applicant's planner said wider, shallower lots reflect market research on smaller yards, add green space along the street and leave more room for on-street parking. One councillor asked why several standard subdivision agreement conditions were removed, and staff said they did not apply, for example heritage resources on a former quarry. The councillor asked that a park design and grading condition be kept, and the committee agreed to refer that suggestion to Council for staff to discuss with the applicant.

Residents opposing the Stanley Avenue development cited traffic, density, strain on water and sewer service, tree removal and cemetery safety. They said the traffic study dated from the pandemic period and left out Bridge Street. They also asked for assurances that no pathway would ever run through the cemetery.

Councillors broadly shared the traffic concern about the Bridge Street bridge and roundabout, including emergency response times. Staff said the Region is responsible for those roads and raised no concerns, and that the City's and Region's mobility master plans are the tools for major improvements. One councillor asked for more comprehensive traffic work covering all area development.

Councillors also pressed on the lack of on-site parkland, tree compensation and sustainability measures. Staff said parkland dedication would likely be taken as cash for the nearby park, that fencing and compensation planting can be required through condominium conditions, and that the zoning by-law cannot regulate details such as balconies.

On the climate lens, one councillor asked whether it would add staff workload and cost. Staff said that depends on the framework chosen and that the Clerk's office would assess impacts during the template review. A councillor who sits on the Climate Change and Environment Committee said the original idea of a section in every report was scaled back to avoid work for its own sake.
